title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'équation des lacets' notes. Grothendieck is working inside a profinite group M, with distinguished elements ρ (order 3 type) and σ, where σ² = −1 is central (the SL2(Z)-type situation). Π̂0 is a normal subgroup; in the context it is the profinite fundamental group / free part. The quotient M/Π̂0 is a small finite group containing the central ±1. Characters ε_3 and ε_2 take values in {±1}. The provisional notation is ε_3(σ) = 1 if ε_3 = 1 and ε_3(σ) = σ if ε_3 = −1.

On the previous page (586), Grothendieck defined a set-theoretic section u ↦ (a,b) of sΓ^!_{j,σ} over Z^!_{j,σ} = M^![σ], via (51). He characterised that section by the congruences (52): u ≡ b ≡ ε_3(σ)a mod Π̂0. He then asked whether the section is multiplicative.

The crossed-out opening paragraph sketches a variant. Fibre products over Γ_{ρ,σ} = G_{ρ,σ}/C^+_{ρ,σ} would be replaced by fibre products over the finer quotient G_{ρ,σ}/Π_0. This would give a 'universal' object and a degree-12 covering of it; 12 is presumably the order of SL2(Z)^ab.

The computation. Take u ↔ (a, b, ε_3) and u' ↔ (a', b', ε_3'). Put u'' = u'u ↔ (a'', b'' = b'b, ε_3'' = ε_3'ε_3). By (52):
- u ≡ ε_3(σ)a
- u' ≡ ε_3'(σ)a'
- u'' ≡ ε_3''(σ)a''

Moreover ε_3''(σ) = ε·ε_3'(σ)ε_3(σ), with ε = −1 exactly when ε_3 = ε_3' = −1, because σ·σ = σ² = −1. Comparing u'' with the product (ε_3'(σ)a')(ε_3(σ)a) and cancelling ε_3'(σ) gives a'·ε_3(σ)a ≡ ε·ε_3(σ)a''. Using that ε is central, this becomes a'' ≡ ε·[ε_3(σ)-conjugate of a']·a. The NB notes that conjugation by σ and by σ^{-1} agree mod Π̂0, since σ² is central.

The a's lie in N'_ρ, which presumably meets Π̂0 trivially. So the desired multiplicativity a'' = a'a is equivalent to a'' ≡ a'a mod Π̂0, hence to condition (54): ε_3(σ)(a') ≡ ε·a' mod Π̂0.

The case split (54 bis), in the margin:
- ε_3 = 1: the condition is trivial, whatever ε_3' is (then ε = 1).
- ε_3 = −1, ε_3' = 1: σ(a') ≡ a', i.e. σ(u') ≡ u'.
- ε_3 = −1, ε_3' = −1: σ(a') ≡ −a', i.e. σ(u') ≡ −u'.

On the next page this is recast as [σ̇, u̇'] = ε_3'. Compared with the earlier relation (35), [σ̇, u̇'] = ε_2(u'), multiplicativity becomes equivalent to ε_2(u') = ε_3(u').

In short, the page computes the obstruction (a ±1-valued 2-cocycle-type term) to the set-theoretic section being a homomorphism.
errors: No genuine error. One step is left implicit: going from a'ε_3(σ)a ≡ εε_3(σ)a'' to a'' ≡ εε_3(σ)(a')·a requires ε to be central and ε_3(σ)(·) to mean conjugation by ε_3(σ)^{-1}. The marginal NB (σ and σ^{-1} act alike mod Π̂0) covers the second point.

The opening paragraph is entirely crossed out, and the final sentence 'Cette condition est automatiquement vérifiée' is left unfinished. The next page shows it is not automatic in general: it reduces to ε_2(u') = ε_3(u').

ideas.what: Testing whether a set-theoretic section of a group extension is multiplicative, by reducing modulo a normal subgroup and isolating a central ±1 sign obstruction coming from σ² = −1
ideas.modern_name: obstruction to splitting / 2-cocycle of a central extension by ±1 (SL2 versus PSL2 type)

ideas.what: Replacing fibre products over G/C^+ by fibre products over the finer quotient G/Π_0, yielding a universal object and a degree-12 covering
ideas.modern_name: covering associated with SL2(Z)^ab ≅ Z/12 / refinement of level structure in the Teichmüller-tower / GT setting
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to themes in La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); unsure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification inside a long computation: a case analysis of a sign obstruction to multiplicativity of a section. Its interest is local to Grothendieck's own construction in the loop-equation notes. The only slightly suggestive element, the degree-12 covering idea, is crossed out and only sketched.
transcription_corrections: The vertical '||' and '≡' symbols between lines record that u'' = u'u ≡ (ε_3'(σ)a')(ε_3(σ)a). The line 'u'u ≡ ε·ε_3'(σ)ε_3(σ)·a''' is the expansion of ε_3''(σ)a''.
Marginal case labels: case 1) ε_3 = ε_3' = 1 is marked 'trivial' (OK). Case 2) is 'ε_3 = 1, ε_3' = −1', also 'trivial', which is consistent with (55a) on the next page.
In the crossed-out first paragraph, 'les [?] lacs [?] universel' is uncertain; the word may be 'le [groupe/lacet] universel'. The 'revêtement de degré 12' reading seems right.
The first line reads 'Soient maintenant u, correspondant à a, b, ε_3 et u', correspondant à a', b', ε_3', et soit u'' = u'u, correspondant à a'', b'' = b'b et ε_3'' = ε_3'ε_3'.
